qa.answer: Four options. Split the bracket line 50/50 with Bengaluru Aero Machining (USD 2K, no slip, recommended), resource both lines to Bengaluru and Laem Chabang Precision (USD 7.5K, no slip), pay Kemuning early for a 2% discount (saves about USD 3K but does not fix its lender problem), or hold and monitor (free until 10 Oct, then exposed).

Early payment on goods receipt is cheapest: a 2% discount on USD 167K saves about USD 3K. It helps only if Kemuning's lender grants the waiver, and it does nothing for WO-2611 if production stops. Of the options that protect WO-2611 whatever happens, the cheapest is the recommended 50/50 split at USD 2K.

In 2023 Kemuning, the same Johor machine shop, entered administration with 22 open lines of brackets and housings (PRE-02). We resourced to Bengaluru within 6 weeks for USD 64K and two inductions absorbed a 9 day slip in float. The lesson was that machined brackets requalify in 6 weeks, so first article should start the day the credit alert lands.

No induction moves yet. WO-2611 needs 30 compressor case brackets at its 12 Nov induction, and Kemuning's slipping line lands 20 Nov, 8 days late against 12 days of float. If Kemuning stops shipping after 10 Oct, a 45 day Bengaluru reorder would land after the 24 Nov float end and Coralline Air's redelivery would move.
